title: db_integration_test TC-DB-03-02: segmentation fault in pg.Conn.close()/deinit after transaction rollback, not the previously-suspected Windows INVALID_HANDLE noise
symptom: GH-652/ISS-0647's own filing described this file's failure as 'INVALID_HANDLE (Windows conn-handle), reproduces consistently' -- a connection-lifecycle signature. Re-measured in true isolation via the new `zig build test-integration-db-integration` narrow step: the actual failure is a hard SEGMENTATION FAULT (not a returned error), captured with a full stack trace: `Segmentation fault at address 0x281fafe1000`, unwinding through `free__anon_34564 -> close -> deinit -> test.TC-DB-03-02: failed transaction rolls back both writes atomically -> mainServer -> main`. This is memory corruption / a double-free or use-after-free inside the vendored pg client's connection-close path (vendor/pg/pg.zig), triggered specifically by TC-DB-03-02's failed-transaction-rollback scenario. 6 of the file's 7 tests pass; only TC-DB-03-02 crashes, and it crashes the whole test binary (SIGSEGV) rather than failing an assertion, so Zig's test runner cannot even report it as a normal test failure -- it shows as '6 pass, 1 crash (7 total)' in the build summary.
acceptance_criteria: Root-cause the segfault: use a memory debugger (e.g. Dr. Memory, or a Linux run under valgrind/ASan if cross-platform reproduction is easier) to find the exact double-free/use-after-free in pg.Conn.close()/deinit reached via TC-DB-03-02's failed-transaction-rollback path

Determine whether this is Windows-specific (the original filing's INVALID_HANDLE guess may still be a contributing factor -- Windows socket/handle double-close behaves differently than POSIX) or a genuine cross-platform memory-safety bug in the vendored pg client
Fix without weakening any existing connection-pool safety invariant (see ISS-0162 / GH-486, ISS-0602 / GH-414 -- this vendor path has a history of subtle cross-connection lifecycle bugs)
TC-DB-03-02 passes in isolation without crashing, twice consecutively
The other 6 tests in db_integration_test.zig must not regress
zig build test exits 0 with unit-test pass count >= established baseline (1011/1075, 64 skipped)
next_action: File as GitHub issue and add to global queue with BLOCKER severity (segfaults in the connection layer are a platform-stability risk, not just a test-flakiness annoyance). This needs a dedicated ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis pass with a memory debugger, not a superficial patch -- the original GH-652 filing's classification of this as Windows connection-handle noise was itself incorrect (re-measurement in true isolation shows a hard crash, not a returned error), so the next investigator should not assume it is environmental.
resolution:
Root-caused WITHOUT needing an external memory debugger -- the stack trace itself (free__anon_34564 -> close -> deinit -> test.TC-DB-03-02) already pinpointed the exact call chain, and reading TC-DB-03-02's own source revealed the bug directly: the test calls `h_phase1.deinit()` explicitly inside its Phase 1 block (line ~470, to force early teardown before Phase 2 opens a second harness) AND ALSO had `defer h_phase1.deinit();` registered at declaration time -- so deinit() (which calls TestHarness.conn.close(), which unconditionally frees vendor/pg/pg.zig's Conn.reader.interface.buffer with no re-entrancy guard anywhere in the chain) ran TWICE on the same harness. The second close() freed an already-freed buffer, corrupting the allocator and segfaulting inside free()'s internal memset (a debug-allocator safety feature that writes `undefined` over freed memory -- the very thing that made this crash instead of silently corrupting something else). This is a plain double-free in the TEST's own code, not a Windows-handle issue and not a genuine bug in the vendored pg client -- vendor/pg/pg.zig and tests/integration/helpers.zig (TestHarness.deinit()) are both UNTOUCHED by this fix, satisfying the issue's own 'do not weaken pool safety invariants' criterion trivially (nothing in the safety-invariant-bearing code changed at all).

Fixed by removing the redundant `defer h_phase1.deinit();` and relying solely on the explicit call inside the Phase 1 block -- this exact 'close early, open a second harness, no defer' pattern already exists correctly elsewhere in the same file (TC-DB-01-02's h1/h2), confirming this is the established, intentional convention for this shape and TC-DB-03-02 was simply the one place that violated it.

Incidental fix in the same file, discovered while re-verifying a clean full pass: TC-DB-03-01's `store.append()` call had no `defer result.record.deinit(alloc)` -- harmless before ISS-0653/GH-662's fix (duplicateFromParams() used to hardcode .metadata="", a zero-length no-op to free), but GH-662's fix (merged just before this run) made .metadata a real allocation, unmasking this as a genuine 1-allocation leak. Fixed alongside since it's the same build target and blocks a clean `zig build test-integration-db-integration` pass.

Verification: zig build test-integration-db-integration -- 7/7 pass, 0 leaks, re-run 5 consecutive times, zero crashes (previously: hard SIGSEGV on TC-DB-03-02 on every run). zig build exits 0, no error-set output. lint_sql_param_types.py 0 findings. lint_test_isolation.py OK, 135 files. zig build test (full unit suite) 89/89 steps, 1011/1075 pass (64 skipped), unchanged from session baseline.
